instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Managed IT services provider offering helpdesk, network management, cybersecurity monitoring, and cloud migration services to 150+ SME clients. 24/7 NOC with 18 technicians. Currently developing a self-service client portal for ticket tracking and automated health reporting. Operate from 2-3 locations or departments. We have some budget headroom for experimentation but look for quick wins that can demonstrate value within 6 months before committing to longer-term programs. The leadership team is aligned on the need to modernize but debates where to start.
answers.pastInitiatives: We piloted a cloud-based project management tool last year, but adoption was inconsistent across teams and we ultimately reverted to spreadsheets and email for most project tracking. The experience highlighted that tool adoption requires more structured change management than we initially planned for.
answers.strategicGoals: Customer retention has declined from 92% to 84% over the past 18 months, primarily among our mid-tier and enterprise segments. Exit interviews consistently cite product stagnation and poor digital self-service tools as reasons for leaving. We need to urgently modernize our customer-facing technology and proactively address the specific pain points driving churn before the trend becomes irreversible.
answers.teamSize: We have a small technology team of 4-6 people including developers, a part-time DevOps engineer, and a product manager who also handles project management. The team is fully allocated to maintaining current products and handling integration requests from key clients. Innovation work is done in the margins — there is no formally ring-fenced innovation time or budget.

input.changes_since_last: Major competitor entered our market. Customer churn rising. Need to accelerate digital transformation.

opportunities.title: Structured Digital Client Self-Service & Retention Program
opportunities.rationale: To counter rising churn and competitive pressure, the current focus must shift from merely building a portal to implementing structured usage that drives proactive customer engagement. This evolution requires linking portal features directly to retention metrics (e.g., automated health reporting triggered by low utilization rates).

first_actions: Define the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) scope focused solely on high-churn segments' top 3 pain points.
Integrate proactive alerts into the portal based on service usage patterns, rather than just passive ticket submission.
Pilot feature rollout with a dedicated group of mid-tier clients to gather structured feedback before full release.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in Net Promoter Score (NPS) detractors attributed to 'digital experience' within 6 months.
milestones: Completion of MVP scope definition and stakeholder sign-off.
Successful integration with NOC data feeds.

opportunities.title: Operational Playbook & Knowledge Transfer Framework
opportunities.rationale: The current reliance on key individuals and informal processes creates critical single points of failure (SPOFs), severely limiting scalability. Formalizing core IT service delivery playbooks ensures business continuity and allows the small team to handle increased load without burnout.

first_actions: Identify 3-5 high-touch, frequently requested services that require standardized operational procedures (SOPs).
Implement a structured knowledge base (wiki) and allocate dedicated time for technical staff to document current best practices.
Develop mandatory quarterly cross-training modules for core support roles.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in resolution time (MTTR) for top 5 recurring issues by documenting and utilizing standardized runbooks.
milestones: Completion of SOPs for the top 3 services.

next_steps.action: Conduct a granular Root Cause Analysis (RCA) of the 84% churn data, segmenting losses specifically by product stagnation vs. poor digital experience.
Formalize the project scope and resource allocation for Opp_1 (Self-Service Portal), securing dedicated engineering time outside of maintenance backlogs.
Host a cross-departmental workshop to identify and prioritize the top 5 most critical operational processes that require documentation and standardization.

key_weaknesses: Lack of ring-fenced time/budget for innovation, forcing efforts into reactive maintenance mode.
High operational risk due to critical reliance on key individuals (single points of failure).
Adoption gap: Past tech tool failures indicate that process governance and change management must precede deployment.

improvements: The company has successfully crystallized the primary pain point driving churn, identifying poor digital self-service tools as a major factor.
Self-service portal development is underway, moving beyond conceptualization to active MVP building.
Leadership alignment on modernization is higher than previously assessed.
persistent_gaps: Process maturity remains low, creating operational drag and slowing the implementation of new digital features.
Team capacity constraint: The core team remains fully allocated to reactive client maintenance, severely limiting proactive innovation time.
Lack of formal process ownership or dedicated documentation structure.
achieved_milestones: Defined clear target metric for customer retention improvement (NPS/churn reduction).
Established basic development track for the self-service portal MVP.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: The assessment reflects a shift from generalized digital transformation discussions to concrete market defense strategies focused on customer retention and addressing specific process bottlenecks caused by high competitive pressure.
